status: PROVISIONAL - all ratio, threshold and clamp values in this file are calibration candidates, not final production values

reference.note: 4K60 reference configuration. The base profiles in x265.json are tuned for this. Scaling factors are computed relative to these values.

classification.note: Metadata-only source-efficiency indicator. This is NOT a GOP detector and makes no frame-type claims.
classification.intra_like_note: INTRA_LIKE currently triggers only on intra-only codec families. H.264/HEVC sources are never classified INTRA_LIKE in this phase (no genuine All-I test source available yet).

thresholds.status: PROVISIONAL - calibrate against real corpus. Reference points: 4K60 150Mbps XAVC HS ~= 0.30, 1080p30 10Mbps ~= 0.16, 1080p30 5Mbps ~= 0.08, 4K60 600Mbps All-I ~= 1.21

param_rules._comment: Modes: fixed (default for anything not listed), fps (FR* expressions evaluated against source fps), sqrt_pixels (scaled by spatial factor), pixel_rate (scaled by pixel-rate factor). Everything not listed here stays fixed to the base profile value (crf/rd/psy/aq/etc. are intentionally never scaled).

rc_lookahead.note: FR* from base profile, ceil(fps * factor), then capped. Cap bounds x265 memory on high-FPS sources (32 GB RAM target).

merange.status: PROVISIONAL clamp bounds - prevent 8K search-complexity explosion; calibrate on real 6K/8K material later

dynamic_vbv._comment: vbv_maxrate_kbps = clamp(OB * target_ratio, OB * min_ratio, OB * max_ratio); vbv_bufsize_kbps = round(maxrate * bufsize_factor). OB = original container bitrate in kbps. CRF remains the primary quality control; maxrate is a local bitrate ceiling, bufsize is the VBV buffer constraint. Missing class entry falls back to the static base-profile VBV.
